findings.passage: The mental health exclusion for possessing a firearm can cause a person or their family to not seek treatment,” Nelson said. “We need to remove this barrier to help.
findings.note: Quoted in a House caucus release when the Judiciary Committee reported his bill. He argues the lifetime gun ban after an emergency mental health commitment keeps people from seeking help.
subjects: who may have a gun (mental health holds)

findings.passage: For some, decades have passed since they received important mental health care,” Nelson said. “They are on firm footing now and should no longer have a lifetime ban. For others, they will continue to need mental health assistance and should not possess a firearm. My bill strikes a balance between the two.
findings.note: Says people recovered from a mental health crisis should not face a lifetime ban, while those who still need care should not have a gun.
subjects: who may have a gun (mental health holds)

findings.note: House Bill 2463 (2017-18 session): per the release, he sponsored it. It would end the permanent gun ban for people given emergency involuntary mental health treatment, replace it with a six-month ban, set a process to restore rights, and require State Police to send relevant records to the national background check system within 72 hours. Date is the committee report date, not the introduction date. The official bill page was blocked, so the id uses the session's first year per store convention.
subjects: who may have a gun (mental health holds)
